Then a certain Kurd whose name was Barkipa,
riding a swift horse,
wearing a coat of mail,
and with a spear in his right hand,
headed straight
toward the hill.
And the Dux supposed
that he was coming to ask for a pledge of safe conduct for his life and for his people,
and took no care regarding him.
And when he drew near,
he struck the Dux with the spear,
pierced the coat of mail,
stabbed him between his ribs, and he died.
And when those who were with him were bewildered over him,
seeing that he had fallen from his horse,
the Kurd fled to his people.
And the cry arose that the Domesticus was killed.
And the Arabs turned back
and captured the son of the Dux,
and later sold him for six thousand dinars.
And ten thousand of the Romans were killed,
and their heads were brought to Egypt.
And the Arabs went immediately to the territory of Antioch,
and they took captives, killed, and burned the villages.
And they returned again to Damascus and took control of it,
because until now it had been under the rule of the Baghdadis.
In this year,
a certain man of the Arabs whose name was 'Allaqah
rebelled in the city of Tyre and took refuge with the Romans.
And the army of the Egyptians overpowered him,
and they seized him and brought him to Egypt.
And they flayed him while alive,
stuffed his skin with straw,
and impaled him.
And at that time,
there were two distinguished Christian men in the city of Daquq,
and they had great authority over it and over its district.
And when a general of the Persians came whose name was Gabriel son of Muhammad,
as he was going to raid in the territory of the Romans,
the Arabs went out to him and said to him:
"Why do you need to go far away? Behold, among us are two Christians who do worse to us than what the Romans would have done to us
if they had ruled over us.
Therefore, show your might, if you can!"
And when he was filled with zeal, he entered the city,
killed them both,
and took control of the city on his own authority,
yet with the consent of its people.
And he was named Dabbus (Tawfus?) al-Dawlah,
that is, the Mace of the Realm.
